study type: Prospective cross-sectional observational study with a 3-month postpartum follow-up for a subset
cohort: The study included 264 women invited for their first vaginal birth, with 52 undergoing ultrasound during the second stage of labor and 35 of 45 vaginally-birthing women attending a 3-month postpartum follow-up.
finding: The study found a significant increase in levator ani muscle (LAM) anteroposterior diameter and hiatal area as the fetal head descended, with LAM avulsions not present during the second stage of labor but diagnosed in 29% of vaginally-birthing women at three months postpartum.
mod_finding: An unsuccessful vaginal delivery followed by Caesarean section was not associated with LAM avulsion, unlike vaginal birth which resulted in a 29% avulsion rate postpartum.
cross-section timing: in the second stage of labour when they had a vaginal examination
